newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for June 10.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for June 10.

text.p: All Mexican ports were open to large ships on Tuesday despite the formation of Tropical Storm Blanca off the country's Pacific coast, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its daily report.
The SCT warned ships of high winds and waves along the coasts of Guerrero, Chiapas and Oaxaca because of the brewing storm, which was updated early Tuesday from a tropical depression.
The ports of Puerto Escondido, Puerto Angel, Huatulco, Salina Cruz and Puerto Madero were closed to minor vessels, namely fishing and tourist boats, the SCT said.
The ministry updated weather conditions and shipping warnings for the Pacific Coast, Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean.
The second weather system of the hurricane season has formed off the country's soutthern Pacific coast. Blanca was upgraded Tuesday to a tropical storm from a tropical depression.
Blanca is currently located 75 miles (120 km) east southeast of the resort of Acapulco and slowly moving west, northwestly, tracking the Guerrero coast, the SCT said.

Light rains expected later in the day on the coasts of Veracruz, Tabasco, Campeche and the Yucatan peninsula. Winds from 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 16 miles per day) and waves three to five feet high.
Hot and partly cloudy with rains and strong winds in Quintana Roo state. Winds from 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 16 miles per day) and waves three to six feet high.
